As of [2021 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Romanian_census "2021 Romanian census"), with 271,692 inhabitants, Iași is the country's third most populous city.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-RPL2021-5) With a population of 500,668 residents (2018), the Iași [urban area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larger_urban_zone "Larger urban zone") is the second largest in Romania.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-eurostat-19)

As of 2021, the [Iași metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_metropolitan_area "Iași metropolitan area") (which includes Iași and 19 other nearby communities) had a population of 423,154, while [Iași County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_County "Iași County"), with its 760,774 inhabitants, was the [most populous county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Romanian_counties_by_population "List of Romanian counties by population") in Romania (after the Municipality of Bucharest).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-RPL2021-5) Additionally there were 60,000 more residents (mostly students) and thousands of daily commuters.

According to the 2002 census, in Iași there were 109,357 housing units and 320,888 people living within the city proper. Of this population, 98.5% were ethnic [Romanians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanians "Romanians"), while 0.59% were ethnic [Romani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_people_in_Romania "Romani people in Romania"), 0.13% [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jews "Jews"), 0.13% [Greeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greeks "Greeks"), 0.13% [Lipovans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipovans "Lipovans"), 0.08% [Hungarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarians "Hungarians"), 0.05% [Germans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_German "Ethnic German") and 0.39% others.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-census-75) In terms of religion, 92.5% of the population were [Christian Orthodox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church "Eastern Orthodox Church"), 4.9% [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic "Roman Catholic"), other religious groups 2.6%. There are currently almost 10,000 Roman Catholics living in Iași.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-76) There is a debate between historians as to whether the Catholics are originally of Romanian or Hungarian descent.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-77)

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Economy")]

[![Image 47](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/31/Iasi%2C_Public_Garden_Palas_6.jpg/250px-Iasi%2C_Public_Garden_Palas_6.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Iasi,_Public_Garden_Palas_6.jpg)

[Palas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palas_Mall "Palas Mall") commercial and business centre

Iași is an important economic centre in Romania. The local and regional economy relies on [industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_sector "Industrial sector") and [service sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy "Tertiary sector of the economy") institutions and establishments. The most important service sectors are related to education, health care, banking, research, culture, government and tourism.

The city is an important [information technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology "Information technology") sector centre, with the presence of several large multinational companies ([Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon.com "Amazon.com"), [Oracle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_Corporation "Oracle Corporation"), [Continental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_AG "Continental AG"), [Conduent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conduent "Conduent"), [Xerox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xerox "Xerox"), [Accenture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accenture "Accenture"), [Capgemini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capgemini "Capgemini"), [SCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SCC_(Specialist_Computer_Centres) "SCC (Specialist Computer Centres)")) and many other local and foreign companies such as [Bentley Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bentley_Systems "Bentley Systems"), [Bitdefender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitdefender "Bitdefender"), [Comodo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comodo_Group "Comodo Group"), [Endava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endava "Endava"), [Ness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ness_Technologies "Ness Technologies"), [Pentalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentalog "Pentalog"), or [TiVo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TiVo_Inc. "TiVo Inc.") (to name a few),[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-78) as well as two universities which offer specific degree programmes. Industry forecasts expect the Iași ITC workforce to grow from the current 16,000 (end of 2016) employees to more than 33,000, by 2030.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-fum-79)

An estimated workforce of more than 35,000 employees is active in Iași's [industrial manufacturing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manufacturing "Manufacturing") sector,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-80) particularly in automotive ([Delphi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delphi_Corporation "Delphi Corporation"), [Lear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lear_Corporation "Lear Corporation"), Conex Distribution), pharmaceutical industry ([Antibiotice Iași](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibiotice_Ia%C8%99i "Antibiotice Iași"), Fiterman Pharma, Ircon SRL), metallurgical production ([ArcelorMittal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ArcelorMittal "ArcelorMittal"), Technosteel LBR), aerospace ([BMT Aerospace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGW "IGW")), industrial equipment (Agmus, ASAM, Fortus), energy ([E.ON Moldova Distribuție](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.ON "E.ON"), [Veolia Energie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veolia "Veolia")), textiles and clothing ([Benetton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Group "Benetton Group"), Iași Conf, Iașitex), home appliances ([Tehnoton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehnoton "Tehnoton")), building materials (Brikston, Build Corp), food (Compan, Panifcom, Zeelandia).[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-industria-55)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-81)

Located in an area recognised for its vineyards and wines, Iași is part of a traditional [wine region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_wine "Romanian wine") with viticultural centres surrounding the city: Copou, Bucium, Uricani, Comarna, Plugari, and Probota. Iași County is also home to renowned [Cotnari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotnari "Cotnari") and [Bohotin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busuioac%C4%83_de_Bohotin "Busuioacă de Bohotin") vineyards.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-83)

With large shopping malls and commercial centres located in the area, Iași also has a well-developed [retail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retail "Retail") business.

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Culture")]

Alecu Balș House, where [Franz Liszt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Liszt "Franz Liszt") performed in 1847, nowadays [Moldova State Philharmonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_%22Moldova%22_Philharmonic_Orchestra "Iași \"Moldova\" Philharmonic Orchestra")

Major events in the political and cultural history of Moldavia are connected with the name of the city of Iași. The great scholars of the 17th century, [Grigore Ureche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grigore_Ureche "Grigore Ureche"), [Miron Costin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miron_Costin "Miron Costin") and later [Ion Neculce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion_Neculce "Ion Neculce"), wrote most of their works in the city or not far from it and the famous scholar [Dimitrie Cantemir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimitrie_Cantemir "Dimitrie Cantemir") known throughout all Europe also linked his name to the capital of Moldavia.

The first newspaper in Romanian was published in 1829 in Iași and it is in Iași where, in 1867, appeared under literary society [Junimea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junimea "Junimea"), the [Convorbiri Literare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convorbiri_Literare "Convorbiri Literare") review in which [Ion Creangă](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion_Creang%C4%83_(writer) "Ion Creangă (writer)")’s [Childhood Memories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childhood_Memories_(Creang%C4%83) "Childhood Memories (Creangă)") and the best poems by [Mihai Eminescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihai_Eminescu "Mihai Eminescu") were published. The reviews [Contemporanul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporanul "Contemporanul") and [Viața Românească](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via%C5%A3a_Rom%C3%A2neasc%C4%83 "Viaţa Românească") appeared in 1871, respectively in 1906 with great contributions to promoting Romanian national cultural values.

Many great personalities of Romanian culture are connected to Iași: the chronicler [Nicolae Milescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolae_Milescu "Nicolae Milescu"), the historians and politicians [Mihail Kogălniceanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihail_Kog%C4%83lniceanu "Mihail Kogălniceanu") and [Simion Bărnuțiu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simion_B%C4%83rnu%C5%A3iu "Simion Bărnuţiu"), the poets [Vasile Alecsandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Alecsandri "Vasile Alecsandri") and [George Topârceanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Top%C3%A2rceanu "George Topârceanu"), the writers [Mihail Sadoveanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihail_Sadoveanu "Mihail Sadoveanu"), [Alecu Russo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alecu_Russo "Alecu Russo"), and [Ionel Teodoreanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionel_Teodoreanu "Ionel Teodoreanu"), the literary critic [Titu Maiorescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titu_Maiorescu "Titu Maiorescu"), the historian [A.D. Xenopol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.D._Xenopol "A.D. Xenopol"), the philosophers [Vasile Conta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Conta "Vasile Conta") and [Petre Andrei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petre_Andrei "Petre Andrei"), the sociologist [Dimitrie Gusti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimitrie_Gusti "Dimitrie Gusti"), the geographer [Emil Racoviță](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Racovi%C5%A3%C4%83 "Emil Racoviţă") and the painter [Octav Băncilă](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octav_B%C4%83ncil%C4%83 "Octav Băncilă"), only to name a few.

The building, designed according to the plans of the Viennese architects [Hermann Helmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Helmer "Hermann Helmer") and [Ferdinand Fellner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Fellner "Ferdinand Fellner"), was raised between 1894 and 1896, and also hosts, starting 1956, the [Iași Romanian National Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_National_Opera,_Ia%C8%99i "Romanian National Opera, Iași").

Iași is home to many museums, memorial houses, and art galleries.

The first memorial museum from Romania opened in Iași in 1918, as the [Ion Creangă](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion_Creang%C4%83_(writer) "Ion Creangă (writer)") Memorial House, and today the [Iași National Museum of Romanian Literature](https://www.muzeulliteraturiiiasi.ro/) owns several memorial houses and museums. The [Mihai Eminescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihai_Eminescu "Mihai Eminescu") Museum, situated in [Copou Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copou_Park "Copou Park"), is dedicated to the great poet's life and creation; other museums are dedicated to: [Dosoftei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dosoftei "Dosoftei"), [Mihail Kogălniceanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihail_Kog%C4%83lniceanu "Mihail Kogălniceanu"), [Vasile Alecsandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Alecsandri "Vasile Alecsandri"), [Mihai Codreanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihai_Codreanu "Mihai Codreanu"), [Vasile Pogor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Pogor "Vasile Pogor"), [Otilia Cazimir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otilia_Cazimir "Otilia Cazimir"), [Mihail Sadoveanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihail_Sadoveanu "Mihail Sadoveanu"), [George Topîrceanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Top%C3%AErceanu "George Topîrceanu"), [Nicolae Gane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolae_Gane "Nicolae Gane"), [Constantin Negruzzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantin_Negruzzi "Constantin Negruzzi"), [Garabet Ibrăileanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garabet_Ibr%C4%83ileanu "Garabet Ibrăileanu"), [Ionel Teodoreanu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionel_Teodoreanu "Ionel Teodoreanu"), [Petru Poni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petru_Poni "Petru Poni"), [Radu Cernătescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radu_Cern%C4%83tescu?action=edit&redlink=1 "Radu Cernătescu (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radu%20Cern%C4%83tescu "ro:Radu Cernătescu")], [Cezar Petrescu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cezar_Petrescu "Cezar Petrescu"), and [Dimitrie Anghel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimitrie_Anghel "Dimitrie Anghel").

The [Theatre Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Romanian_Theatre_Collection?action=edit&redlink=1 "History of Romanian Theatre Collection (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colec%C8%9Bia%20Muzeal%C4%83%20%E2%80%9EIstoria%20teatrului%20rom%C3%A2nesc%E2%80%9D%20din%20Ia%C8%99i "ro:Colecția Muzeală „Istoria teatrului românesc” din Iași")], opened in 1976 at the celebration of 160 years since the first theatrical performance in Romanian, illustrates the development of the theatrical phenomenon since the beginning, important moments of the history of Iași National Theatre, the foundation, in 1840, of the Philharmonic-dramatic Conservatoire, prestigious figures that have contributed to the development of the Romanian theatre.

The [Union Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Museum,_Ia%C8%99i?action=edit&redlink=1 "Union Museum, Iași (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muzeul%20Unirii%20din%20Ia%C8%99i "ro:Muzeul Unirii din Iași")], includes original pieces and documents which belonged to prince [Al. I. Cuza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al._I._Cuza "Al. I. Cuza") and his family.

The [Museum of Natural History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_Museum_of_Natural_History?action=edit&redlink=1 "Iași Museum of Natural History (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muzeul%20de%20Istorie%20Natural%C4%83%20din%20Ia%C8%99i "ro:Muzeul de Istorie Naturală din Iași")], founded on 4 February 1834, is the first museum of this kind in Romania with over 300,000 items, the most valuable being the collections of insects, mollusc, amphibians, reptiles, birds, plants and minerals.

Four other museums are located in the [Palace of Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Culture_(Ia%C5%9Fi) "Palace of Culture (Iaşi)"): with its roots dating back to 1860, the _Iași Art Museum_ is the oldest of its kind in Romania,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-88) and, with more than 8,700 works (many of them belonging to the universal patrimony), has the largest art collection in the country; the _Moldavia's History Museum_, offers more than 48,000 objects from various fields, archaeology, numismatics, decorative art, ancient books, documents; the _Ethnographic Museum of Moldavia_ owns more than 13,000 objects depicting the Romanian advance through the ages; the _Science and Technology Museum's_ collection has more than 11,200 objects in five distinct sections and one memorial house.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-ra-89)

In May 2016, the [Iași Municipal Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_Municipal_Museum?action=edit&redlink=1 "Iași Municipal Museum (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muzeul%20Municipal%20din%20Ia%C8%99i "ro:Muzeul Municipal din Iași")] was re-established, while in July 2021 four new museums, located in the House of Museums, were opened to the public: the Museum of Iași Pogrom, the Museum of the Jewish Theatre in Romania, the Museum of Poetry, and the Museum of Childhood under Communism.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-90) Iași is home to the Gheorghe Asachi Technical University Library, voted the most beautiful library in the world in a 2015 online poll. The library is situated within the historical University Palace, a building designed by architects Louis Blanc and Petru Poni, who drew inspiration from prominent European academic architecture.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-91)

### Cultural events and festivals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Cultural events and festivals")]

*   FIE (_International Education Festival_), launched in 2013, is a mix of cultural and educative events;
*   _International Theatre Festival for Young Audience_ was launched in 2008 and it is hosted each October by [Luceafărul Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luceaf%C4%83rul_Theatre_(Ia%C8%99i) "Luceafărul Theatre (Iași)");
*   Since 2010 at SFR(Romanian Film Nights) are presented films from different periods of Romanian cinema, as well as new films, debut films or short films, with the invitation of actors, directors, scriptwriters and film critics in the projection;
*   [FILIT](https://www.filit-iasi.ro/) (_International Festival of Literature and Translation_) is a yearly literature and translation festival organised through the Iași Museum of Romanian Literature, begun in 2013;
*   Started in 2017, afterhills is the biggest music festival in Moldavia. Other music festivals: Rock'n'Iași since 2007 and Rocanotherworld since 2016.
*   Hangariada is an aeronautics and art festival organised each year in May;

Live music and different other artistic events (poetry nights, readings) are a habitual occurrence in the various bars and coffee shops the city has to offer.

[Central University Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_University_Library_of_Ia%C8%99i "Central University Library of Iași")

The first institute of higher learning that functioned on the territory of Romania was [Academia Vasiliană](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasilian_College "Vasilian College") (1640) founded by Prince [Vasile Lupu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Lupu "Vasile Lupu") as a "higher school for Latin and Slavonic languages," followed by the [Princely Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_Academy,_Ia%C5%9Fi "Princely Academy, Iaşi") in 1707.

The first high education structure in [Romanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_language "Romanian language") was established in the autumn of 1813, when engineer [Gheorghe Asachi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gheorghe_Asachi "Gheorghe Asachi") laid the foundations of a class of engineers, its activities taking place within the [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language") Hegemonic School.

After 1813, other moments marked the development of higher education in Romanian, regarding both [humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanities "Humanities") and the technical science. In 1835, [Academia Mihăileană](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academia_Mih%C4%83ilean%C4%83 "Academia Mihăileană") founded by [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_rulers_of_Moldavia "List of rulers of Moldavia")[Mihail Sturdza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihail_Sturdza "Mihail Sturdza") is considered first Romanian superior institute in the country.

[![Image 58](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Ia%C5%9Fi_%2C_Faculty_of_Electrical_Engineering_%2C_Energetical_and_Applied_Informatics_3.jpg/250px-Ia%C5%9Fi_%2C_Faculty_of_Electrical_Engineering_%2C_Energetical_and_Applied_Informatics_3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ia%C5%9Fi_,_Faculty_of_Electrical_Engineering_,_Energetical_and_Applied_Informatics_3.jpg)

Faculty of Electrical Engineering, [Gheorghe Asachi Technical University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gheorghe_Asachi_Technical_University_of_Ia%C8%99i "Gheorghe Asachi Technical University of Iași")

In 1860, three faculties part of the Academia Mihăileană formed the nucleus for the newly established [University of Iași](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Ia%C5%9Fi "University of Iaşi"), the first Romanian university.

The [Physicians and Naturalists Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physicians_and_Naturalists_Society_(Ia%C8%99i)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Physicians and Naturalists Society (Iași) (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Societatea%20de%20Medici%20%C8%99i%20Naturali%C8%99ti "ro:Societatea de Medici și Naturaliști")], founded in Iași, has existed since the early part of the 19th century, and a number of periodicals are published.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChisholm1911-35) One of the oldest medical universities in Romania, founded in 1879, is located in Iași. It is now known as the [Grigore T. Popa University of Medicine and Pharmacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grigore_T._Popa_University_of_Medicine_and_Pharmacy "Grigore T. Popa University of Medicine and Pharmacy").

In 1937, the two [applied science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applied_science "Applied science") sections of the University of Iași became departments of the newly created [Gheorghe Asachi Polytechnic School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gheorghe_Asachi_Technical_University_of_Ia%C5%9Fi "Gheorghe Asachi Technical University of Iaşi"). In the period before and after [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the later (renamed _Polytechnic Institute_ in 1948) extended its domain of activity, especially in the field of engineering, and became known as Gheorghe Asachi Technical University in 1993.

*   [Grigore T. Popa University of Medicine and Pharmacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grigore_T._Popa_University_of_Medicine_and_Pharmacy "Grigore T. Popa University of Medicine and Pharmacy") – one of the oldest medicine schools in Romania;
*   [George Enescu National University of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Enescu_National_University_of_Arts "George Enescu National University of Arts") – the oldest tradition in music and arts education in Romania;
*   [Ion Ionescu de la Brad University of Life Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_University_of_Life_Sciences "Iași University of Life Sciences") – one of the oldest schools of its kind.

There are also some private higher education institutions including [Petre Andrei University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petre_Andrei_University_of_Ia%C8%99i "Petre Andrei University of Iași"), the largest private university in the historical region of Moldavia.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-92)

The [Central University Library of Iași](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_University_Library_of_Ia%C5%9Fi "Central University Library of Iaşi"), where the chief records of Romanian history are preserved, is the oldest and the second largest in Romania.

As of 2016[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit), Iași has 74 [public schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_school_(government_funded) "Public school (government funded)"), coordinated by the [Iași County School Inspectorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_County_School_Inspectorate?action=edit&redlink=1 "Iași County School Inspectorate (page does not exist)"). The city is also home to 19 private schools.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-93)

Notable high schools:

*   [Iași National College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_National_College "Iași National College") (1828)
*   [Costache Negruzzi National College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costache_Negruzzi_National_College "Costache Negruzzi National College") (1895)
*   [Emil Racoviță National College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Racovi%C8%9B%C4%83_National_College?action=edit&redlink=1 "Emil Racoviță National College (page does not exist)") (1964)
*   [Mihai Eminescu National College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihai_Eminescu_National_College_(Ia%C8%99i)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mihai Eminescu National College (Iași) (page does not exist)") (1865)
*   [Vasile Lupu Pedagogical High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Lupu_Pedagogical_High_School?action=edit&redlink=1 "Vasile Lupu Pedagogical High School (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C8%98coala%20Normal%C4%83%20%E2%80%9EVasile%20Lupu%E2%80%9D%20din%20Ia%C8%99i "ro:Școala Normală „Vasile Lupu” din Iași")] (1855)

Iași Science Festival is a week long festival organised every year in April (starting 2013) for high school and grade school students to get be able to observe and take part in scientific experiments and be given detailed tours of the scientific and technical universities and research labs in Iași. Over 200 experiments were performed and over 10,000 students took part in the 2014 edition, from throughout the Moldavia region.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-94)

## Transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Transport")]

[![Image 62](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Pesa_Swing_122NaJ.jpg/250px-Pesa_Swing_122NaJ.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pesa_Swing_122NaJ.jpg)

The [Iași tram network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trams_in_Ia%C8%99i "Trams in Iași") is the backbone of the city's public transport

### Public transport

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Public transport")]

Iași's public transportation system is served by the [CTP Iași](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CTP_Ia%C8%99i "CTP Iași") (former RATP), which operates an extensive network using 126 [trams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tram "Tram") (electric trams began operating in Iași in 1900) and 150 buses.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-98) In 2014, CTP carried 50,358,000 passengers, an average of 140,000 passengers per day.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-99)

### Air

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Air")]

[![Image 63](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Aeroportul_International_Iasi_2024.jpg/250px-Aeroportul_International_Iasi_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aeroportul_International_Iasi_2024.jpg)

[Iași Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_International_Airport "Iași International Airport") in 2024

Iași is served by the [Iași International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i_International_Airport "Iași International Airport") (IAS) located 8 km (5.0 mi) east of the city centre. The airport is the 3rd busiest in Romania and offers direct domestic, [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union"), and [Middle Eastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East") scheduled or charter connections. After extensive modernisation works, the number of connections and traffic volumes have seen a significant increase since 2015.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-100)

### Rail

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=36 "Edit section: Rail")]

[![Image 64](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Gara_Iasi3.jpg/250px-Gara_Iasi3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gara_Iasi3.jpg)

[Iași Grand Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_railway_station "Iaşi railway station")

Iași-[Pașcani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pa%C8%99cani "Pașcani") railway was opened on 1 June [[O.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Style "Old Style") 20 May] 1870, Iași-[Ungheni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ungheni "Ungheni") on 1 August 1874 and Iași-[Chișinău](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u "Chișinău") railway was opened on 1 June 1875 by the [Russian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire "Russian Empire") in preparation for the [Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Turkish_War_(1877%E2%80%931878) "Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)").

Nowadays, three railway stations, [Grand Railway Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C5%9Fi_railway_station "Iaşi railway station"), [Nicolina International railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolina_International_railway_station?action=edit&redlink=1 "Nicolina International railway station (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gara%20Interna%C8%9Bional%C4%83%20Nicolina "ro:Gara Internațională Nicolina")] and [Socola railway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socola_railway_station?action=edit&redlink=1 "Socola railway station (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gara%20Socola "ro:Gara Socola")] serve the city and are operated by [Romanian Railways](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C4%83ile_Ferate_Rom%C3%A2ne "Căile Ferate Române") (CFR). [Moldovan railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calea_Ferat%C4%83_din_Moldova "Calea Ferată din Moldova") also serves these stations for travel into [Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldova "Moldova").

The Grand Railway Station, located about 1 km (0.6 mi) from the city centre, provides direct rail connections to all the major Romanian cities and to [Chișinău](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u "Chișinău"), Moldova. The rail stations are very well connected to all the parts of the city by the [trams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tram "Tram") and buses of the local public transport companies.

### Road

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Road")]

Iași is connected by European routes E583/[E85](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E85 "European route E85") with [Bucharest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bucharest "Bucharest") through a four lane road, by [European route E58](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_route_E58 "European route E58") with Central Europe and [Chișinău](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u "Chișinău") in [Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldova "Moldova"), and by [DN National Roads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roads_in_Romania "Roads in Romania") with all major cities of Romania. The [East-West Motorway (A8)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East%E2%80%93West_Motorway_(Romania) "East–West Motorway (Romania)") (also known as The Union Motorway), in various stages of construction and planning, which starts at the Romanian border with Moldova in [Ungheni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ungheni,_Ia%C8%99i "Ungheni, Iași"), will connect the city to the [A7 Moldavia Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A7_motorway_(Romania) "A7 motorway (Romania)") in [Pașcani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pa%C8%99cani "Pașcani"), and the [A3 Transylvania Motorway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A3_motorway_(Romania) "A3 motorway (Romania)") near [Târgu Mureș](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C3%A2rgu_Mure%C8%99 "Târgu Mureș").

The Iași Coach Station is used by several private transport companies to provide [coach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coach_(vehicle) "Coach (vehicle)") connections from Iași to a large number of locations from all over the country.

## Health care

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Health care")]

Iași is home to 14 public hospitals, including the [Saint Spiridon Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Spiridon_Hospital?action=edit&redlink=1 "Saint Spiridon Hospital (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spitalul%20Clinic%20Jude%C8%9Bean%20de%20Urgen%C8%9B%C4%83%20%E2%80%9ESf%C3%A2ntul%20Spiridon%E2%80%9D%20Ia%C8%99i "ro:Spitalul Clinic Județean de Urgență „Sfântul Spiridon” Iași")], the second largest and one of the oldest in Romania (1755),[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-101) St. Maria Clinic Children's Hospital (one of the largest children's hospitals in the country), Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases, Regional Oncology Institute, and [Socola Psychiatric Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socola_Psychiatric_Institute?action=edit&redlink=1 "Socola Psychiatric Institute (page does not exist)")[[ro](https://ro.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spitalul%20Clinic%20de%20Psihiatrie%20%E2%80%9ESocola%E2%80%9D "ro:Spitalul Clinic de Psihiatrie „Socola”")] (1905 – first psychiatric hospital in Romania). The public system is complemented by numerous private clinics.

In December 2021, the Ministry of Health signed the contract for the design of a new hospital that will serve the entire [North-East region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nord-Est_(development_region) "Nord-Est (development region)").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-103) The total investment in the construction of the Iași Regional Emergency Hospital ([Romanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_language "Romanian language"): _Spitalul Regional de Urgență (SRU) Iași_), with a completion date of 2027, is estimated at over 500 million euros.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-105)

### Air pollution concerns

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ia%C8%99i&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Air pollution concerns")]

In 2014, the [European Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Commission "European Commission") started environmental law [infringement procedures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infringement_procedure "Infringement procedure") against Romania, citing [Bucharest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bucharest "Bucharest"), Iași, and [Brașov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bra%C8%99ov "Brașov") cases as examples.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-106) In 2015, while the [atmospheric particulate matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particulates "Particulates") has repeatedly reached and exceeded legal thresholds for PM 10, Iași came to be regarded as the city with the second worst air quality in Romania, after Bucharest.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-ro_2016-05-13-107) Pollution from vehicular traffic, construction works, and a lack of green spaces (the city only has about 11 m 2 (118 sq ft) of public green spaces per capita) make up some of the reasons behind these problems.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ia%C8%99i#cite_note-ro_2016-05-13-107)

The **Vasile Alecsandri National Theatre** ([Romanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_language "Romanian language"): _Teatrul Național „Vasile Alecsandri” din Bălți_) in [Bălți](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C4%83l%C8%9Bi "Bălți"), is one of the national theatres of [Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldova "Moldova"). Founded in 1957, it was given the name of the renowned Romanian playwright and poet [Vasile Alecsandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasile_Alecsandri "Vasile Alecsandri"). On 26 January 1990,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C4%83l%C8%9Bi_National_Theatre#cite_note-history-1) Vasile Alecsandri Theatre became the first national theatre in Moldova.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C4%83l%C8%9Bi_National_Theatre#cite_note-2)

**Moldavia** ([Romanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_language "Romanian language"): _Moldova_, pronounced[[molˈdova]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Romanian "Help:IPA/Romanian")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/9/90/Ro-Moldova.ogg/Ro-Moldova.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ro-Moldova.ogg "File:Ro-Moldova.ogg") or _Țara Moldovei_ lit.'The land of Moldova'; in [Romanian Cyrillic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Romanian Cyrillic alphabet"): Мѡлдѡва or Цара Мѡлдѡвєй) is a [historical region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_region "Historical region") and former [principality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality "Principality") in [Eastern Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Europe "Eastern Europe"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-12)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-13)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-14) corresponding to the territory between the [Eastern Carpathians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Carpathians "Eastern Carpathians") and the [Dniester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dniester "Dniester") River. An initially independent and later [autonomous state under Ottoman overlordship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vassal_and_tributary_states_of_the_Ottoman_Empire "Vassal and tributary states of the Ottoman Empire"), it existed from the 14th century to 1859, when it united with [Wallachia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallachia "Wallachia") (_Țara Românească_) as the basis of the modern [Romanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania") state; at various times, Moldavia included the regions of [Bessarabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bessarabia "Bessarabia") (with the [Budjak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budjak "Budjak")), all of [Bukovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bukovina "Bukovina") and [Hertsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertsa_region "Hertsa region"). It also included the region of [Pokuttya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokuttya "Pokuttya") for a period of time.

The [western half of Moldavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Moldavia "Western Moldavia") is now part of Romania, the eastern side belongs to the [Republic of Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldova "Moldova"), and the [northern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chernivtsi_Oblast "Chernivtsi Oblast") and [southeastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budjak "Budjak") parts are territories of Ukraine.

## Name and etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moldavia&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Name and etymology")]

Main article: [Etymology of Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etymology_of_Moldova "Etymology of Moldova")

The original and short-lived reference to the region was _Bogdania_, after [Bogdan I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogdan_I "Bogdan I"), the founding figure of the principality.[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-16)

The names _Moldavia_ and _Moldova_ are derived from the name of the [Moldova River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldova_River "Moldova River"); however, the etymology is not known and there are several variants:[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-17)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-18)

*   A legend mentioned in _[Descriptio Moldaviae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descriptio\_Moldaviae?action=edit&redlink=1 "Descriptio Moldaviae (page does not exist)")_ (1714–1716) by [Dimitrie Cantemir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimitrie_Cantemir "Dimitrie Cantemir") links it to an [aurochs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurochs "Aurochs") hunting trip of the [voivode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voivode "Voivode") of the [Voivodeship of Maramureș](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voivodeship_of_Maramure%C8%99 "Voivodeship of Maramureș")[Dragoș](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drago%C8%99 "Dragoș") and the latter's chase of a star-marked aurochs. Dragoș was accompanied by his female hound, called _Molda_; when they reached the shores of an unfamiliar river, Molda caught up with the animal and was killed by it. The dog's name would have been combined with the Romanian word for water, _apă_, and given to the river and extended to the country.
*   the [Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_language "Gothic language")_Mulda_ ([Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_language "Gothic language"): 𐌼𐌿𐌻𐌳𐌰, ᛗᚢᛚᛞᚨ) meaning 'dust', 'dirt' (cognate with the English _[mould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mold\_(fungus) "Mold (fungus)")_), referring to the river.
*   A [Slavic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavic_languages "Slavic languages") etymology (_-ova_ is a quite common Slavic suffix), marking the end of one Slavic genitive form, denoting ownership, chiefly of feminine nouns (i.e., 'that of Molda').
*   A landowner named Alexa Moldaowicz is mentioned in a 1334 document as a local [boyar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyar "Boyar") in service to [Yuriy II of Halych](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boleslaus_George_II_of_Halych "Boleslaus George II of Halych"); this attests to the use of the name before the foundation of the Moldavian state and could be the source for the region's name.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On a series of coins of [Peter I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petru_I_of_Moldavia "Petru I of Moldavia") and [Stephen I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_I_of_Moldavia "Stephen I of Moldavia") minted by [Saxon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transylvanian_Saxons "Transylvanian Saxons") masters and with German legends, the [reverses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obverse_and_reverse "Obverse and reverse") feature the name of Moldavia in the form _Molderlang_/_Molderlant_ (recte: _Molderland_).[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-LBieltz-19)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-KParvan-20)

In several early references,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-21)_Moldavia_ is rendered under the composite form _Moldo-Wallachia_ (in the same way Wallachia may appear as _Hungro-Wallachia_). [Ottoman Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Turkish_language "Ottoman Turkish language") references to Moldavia included _Boğdan Iflak_ (بغدان افلاق, meaning '[Bogdan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogdan#Rulers_of_Moldavia "Bogdan")'s Wallachia') and _Boğdan_ (and occasionally _Kara-Boğdan_, قره بغدان, "Black Bogdania"). See also [names in other languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_regions_with_alternative_names#M "List of European regions with alternative names").

The names of the region in other languages include [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Moldavie_, [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"): _Moldau_, [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_language "Hungarian language"): _Moldva_, [Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language "Russian language"): Молдавия (_Moldaviya_), [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_language "Turkish language"): _Boğdan Prensliği_, [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language"): Μολδαβία.

### Endonym

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moldavia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Endonym")]

See also: [Controversy over ethnic and linguistic identity in Moldova §Principality of Moldavia (1359–1812)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controversy_over_ethnic_and_linguistic_identity_in_Moldova#Principality_of_Moldavia_(1359%E2%80%931812) "Controversy over ethnic and linguistic identity in Moldova")

According to [Wallachian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallachia "Wallachia") chronicler [Constantin Cantacuzino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantin_Cantacuzino_(stolnic) "Constantin Cantacuzino (stolnic)") (1655–1716)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-22) and a recount by Hungarian traveller [Fedor Karacsay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedor_von_Karacsay?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fedor von Karacsay (page does not exist)")[[tr](https://tr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedor%20Karacsay "tr:Fedor Karacsay")] (1818), the inhabitants of Moldavia referred to themselves as "Moldavians" instead of "Romanians".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-23) However, travellers Francesco della Valle (1532)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-24) and Pierre Lescalopier (1574) claimed the opposite; shared use of endonym "Romanian" by the inhabitants of Wallachia, Transylvania and Moldavia.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-25)

## History

### Prehistory and antiquity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moldavia&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Prehistory and antiquity")]

Main articles: [Prehistory of the Balkans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehistory_of_the_Balkans "Prehistory of the Balkans"), [Cucuteni–Trypillian culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cucuteni%E2%80%93Trypillian_culture "Cucuteni–Trypillian culture"), [Getae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getae "Getae"), [Dacians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacians "Dacians"), [Costoboci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costoboci "Costoboci"), [Carpi (people)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpi_(people) "Carpi (people)"), [Dacia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacia "Dacia"), [Trajan's Dacian Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trajan's_Dacian_Wars "Trajan's Dacian Wars"), and [Roman Dacia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Dacia "Roman Dacia")

### Early Middle Ages

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moldavia&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Early Middle Ages")]

Main articles: [Origin of the Romanians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origin_of_the_Romanians "Origin of the Romanians") and [Romania in the Early Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania_in_the_Early_Middle_Ages "Romania in the Early Middle Ages")

The inhabitants of Moldavia were Christians. Archaeological works revealed the remains of a Christian necropolis at [Mihălășeni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mih%C4%83l%C4%83%C8%99eni,_Boto%C8%99ani "Mihălășeni, Botoșani"), [Botoșani county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boto%C8%99ani_County "Botoșani County"), from the 5th century. The place of worship, and the tombs had Christian characteristics. The place of worship had a rectangular form with sides of eight and seven meters. Similar necropolises and places of worship were found at Nicolina, in Iași[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-26)

The [Bolohoveni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolokhoveni "Bolokhoveni") are mentioned by the _[Hypatian Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypatian\_Codex "Hypatian Codex")_ in the 13th century. The chronicle shows that this[_[which?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid\_weasel\_words "Wikipedia:Avoid weasel words")_] land is bordered on the principalities of Halych, Volhynia and Kiev. Archaeological research also identified the location of 13th-century fortified settlements in this region.[_[which?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid\_weasel\_words "Wikipedia:Avoid weasel words")_] Alexandru V. Boldur identified Voscodavie, Voscodavti, Voloscovti, Volcovti, Volosovca and their other towns and villages between the middle course of the rivers Nistru/Dniester and Nipru/Dnieper.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-27) The Bolohoveni disappeared from chronicles after their defeat in 1257 by [Daniel of Galicia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_of_Galicia "Daniel of Galicia")'s troops. Their ethnic identity is uncertain; although Romanian scholars, basing on their ethnonym identify them as [Romanians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanians "Romanians") (who were called [Vlachs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vlachs "Vlachs") in the [Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages")), archeological evidence and the _[Hypatian Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypatian\_Chronicle "Hypatian Chronicle")_ (which is the only [primary source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_source "Primary source") that documents their history) suggest that they were a [Slavic people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavic_peoples "Slavic peoples").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpinei198657-28)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-Bolokhovians-29)

In the early 13th century, the _[Brodniks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brodnici "Brodnici")_, a possible [Slavic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavs "Slavs")–[Vlach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vlachs "Vlachs")[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][vassal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vassal "Vassal") state of [Halych](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halych-Volhynia "Halych-Volhynia"), were present, alongside the Vlachs, in much of the region's territory (towards 1216, the Brodniks are mentioned as in service of [Suzdal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir-Suzdal "Vladimir-Suzdal")).

Somewhere in the 11th century, a [Viking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking "Viking") named Rodfos [was killed by Vlachs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blakumen "Blakumen") presumably in the area of what would become Moldavia.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldavia#cite_note-30) In 1164, the future [Byzantine emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_Empire "Byzantine Empire")[Andronikos I Komnenos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andronikos_I_Komnenos "Andronikos I Komnenos"), was taken prisoner by Vlach shepherds in the same region.
